context.description: A run resumes only by the same path (owner ruling 3)

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review of verify-spec-SV3.spec.ts (committed, sha256 prefix 179d4e0c9f364c29); my own bun run at HEAD f57285510d: 2 pass, 0 fail, 23 expect(). Everything runs on the real /task command (loader, sliceOf, lease, job, Recorder, supervisors, workers) with the real core BackgroundJob registry in a seeded git instance; only the model side is scripted. I read command.ts sliceOf and job: resume only when the latest slice is not ended and its stored path equals the normalised path. Given a stored slice that has not ended, started by /task with a path: run.started {path: SPEC} and task.started T1.1 (real worktree, session ses_T1.1) published to the real store. When /task runs again with the same path: written ./SPEC/, so normalisation is exercised. Then the slice is folded: status.json shows T1.1 building with attempts 1 and the stored worktree, and the history holds the stored at:2 entry - only the fold of the stored facts can give these; T1.1 is not begun again. run.resumed is recorded with that path: the third stored fact is run.resumed {path: SPEC, base: branch} right after the two stored facts, and there is still one run.started. The supervisor starts what the folded state asks for: T1.1's supervisor claims the stored session (ownerOf = task:<id>:T1.1, watch true) and prompts it again; T1.2, ready in the fold, gets task.started in a new session; T1.3, which waits on T1.1, has no supervisor. A server stop (scope close) leaves the slice open with no run.cancelled. And /task with a different path starts a new slice: the T1.1 folder path while the stored slice is open records run.started with that path, and T1.1 begins again in a new session (a fold from nothing). Or after the slice ended: after a job cancel stores run.cancelled, the same path again records a third run.started; no run.resumed is stored in that test. No gap found for this Gherkin; the done and stored-stop ends are covered by RM8a and RM8c.
